title: Has anyone else ever made a rhythm game?
author: ThinkTyler
selftext:
I’ve been working on a rhythm game for the better part of 4 months in my free time. I am a musician, a designer, and work in vertical AI as a product marketer, so it kinda fits right in.

My stack right now is using Claude, Godot, Blender and Kenney AIO pack, using most of the 3d low poly assets, with Claude modeling in Blender the missing stuff I need. I originally started with LimeZu pixel art pack but moved to low poly recently and I like it a lot more. 

My game is about a local sound guy having enough  and starting his own band, but he has to gain enough exposures to be able to play the big gig and win the game. The overworld is a parody of a main popular strip in the city I live. You music battle various people to progress through the game, kinda like guitar hero meets Scott pilgrim. There’s lots of nuance and IYKYK type of stuff in it, which I’m having a blast being creative with.

Anyway, I am wondering if anyone else has made a rhythm game and what kind of mechanics you did for the music portion?  Like do I build virtual synths and drum machines in game? Do I record a ton of layered loops in an DAW, export them, and make data files for each battle? Or do I just make a bunch of songs and have the player react to that? How should I do the actual controls? Should I do note lanes like guitar hero with a visual hit zone or do more like rhythmic key stroke combos like parappa the rapper?

Would just like to hear your thoughts on this and how you approached it from a mechanics perspective. Not the actual conductor/music timing technical part, but like how it feels and what you think works well and is fun to play.
